answer: A Sybil‑resistant orchard of agents assigns each node a time‑locked umber token that must be refreshed each epoch by submitting a signed proof of work derived from a unique falcon‑seed challenge. The node broadcasts the proof; peers verify the signature and the epoch hash, then extend the node’s liveness window; any node that fails to deliver fresh work automatically expires and its token is burned. An attacker must lock up one umber token per fake identity and expend the full proof‑of‑work each epoch, costing 1 um‑token and the associated compute per cycle.
